item.title: Mount Odaigahara: Nara's Wild Rooftop Wilderness — Guide
item.description: Mount Odaigahara, straddling the Nara–Mie border deep in the Yoshino-Kumano National Park, is one of the wildest and most beautiful high places in western Japan — and one of the rainiest spots in the whole country, which cloaks it in lush, moss-draped primeval forest. A road climbs to a trailhead at around 1,570 metres, from which well-made loop trails (including boardwalks over fragile terrain) lead through ancient woodland, past the dramatic Daijagura cliff viewpoint with its vast panorama, and to the summit of Hidegatake.
